requirements.text: A maximum of 6 hours of credit in CSCE 2900, CSCE 4890, CSCE 4920, CSCE 4940 or CSCE 4950 will count toward this degree. The 6 hours may include at most 3 hours in CSCE 4920.

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.text: Hours required for electives may vary based on course selection and the University Core Curriculum requirements. Electives may be required to satisfy the advanced hour requirement (42) and/or the minimum total hours required for the degree. For specific information see an academic advisor in the College of Engineering. Currently, there should be approximately 15 hours of CSCE electives available.

requirements.name: Communication core grade
requirements.quote: Students must have a grade of C or better in courses that meet the Communication requirement of the University Core Curriculum to show proficiency in English composition. Students who have earned a D in one or more of these two required courses must repeat the course and raise the grade to a C or better. Transfer students with more than 90 hours and who have earned a D in any of the basic English writing courses must retake the course during their first term/semester in residence.

node.name: Option 4
node.text: Students double majoring in mathematics and another discipline (typically biology, chemistry, physics or engineering) that requires at least 12 hours of laboratory science intended for science and engineering majors may use the same laboratory science courses that satisfy the requirements for the other major to satisfy the laboratory science requirement for the mathematics major.

citation.heading: Plus one of the following lecture and laboratory combinations

node.name: Proficiency in a foreign language equivalent to 1020
node.text: Proficiency in a foreign language equivalent to 1020 is required. Students intending to pursue a graduate degree in mathematics are encouraged to study French, German or Russian.

requirements.name: Minor requirements
requirements.text: One of the following is required: A minor of at least 18 hours (6 advanced). A minor in statistics does not fulfill this requirement. Completion of a second major in addition to mathematics. Completion of the actuarial science certificate. Students must take STAT 3680, MATH 4610 and STAT 4650 for fulfilling degree requirements; students are also encouraged to take MATH 3350 and MATH 3740. Also, no mathematics courses may be chosen for fulfilling the elective requirements of the certificate program. Completion of the data analytics certificate.

requirements.name: GPA 2.0 (mathematics courses 3350+ in the major)

requirements.name: Degree requirements
requirements.text: The following requirements must be satisfied for a Bachelor of Science with a major in biology. Foundation Course requirements must be successfully completed prior to advancing to upper-division major requirements.

children.name: Foundation grade rules
children.quote: The Foundation course requirements listed below must be completed before enrollment in 3000 and 4000 level courses required for the major. Successful completion is based on achieving a C or better in each course and an overall 2.5 grade point average in these courses.

children.text: In addition to the biology foundation courses, students must complete with a C or higher a second 2000 level biology course, the advanced biology requirements, one physiology course with laboratory, and 16 advanced biology elective hours (of which 2 courses must be with laboratory).

requirements.name: Electives
requirements.text: Hours required for electives may vary based on course selection and the University Core Curriculum requirements. Electives may be required to satisfy the advanced hour requirement and/or the minimum total hours required for the degree. For specific information see an academic advisor in the College of Science.

requirements.name: Other requirements
requirements.text: Only two attempts will be allowed for each biology and biochemistry course in the degree. Grade of C or better and minimum 2.5 grade point average in Foundation Courses, C or better in all upper-division courses counting towards major requirements, and an overall 2.0 grade point average are required for graduation. All students seeking to enter the Department of Biological Sciences, with the exception of beginning freshmen, must meet the minimum grade point averages given above. Students in the department whose Foundation Course or overall grade point average drops below the minimum for two consecutive semesters will be removed from the program.

requirements.name: Core total: 42 hours
requirements.quote: Students are required to complete 42 semester credit hours in specific areas. Students select core courses to meet the state semester credit hour requirements for each foundational component area. More information about the Core Curriculum at UNT may be found in the UNT Student Success Guidebook on the Advising web site.

children.name: Communication core grade
children.quote: Students must take one course from Group 1 and one course from group 2. The courses are often taken in sequence (for example, students first take ENGL 1310, then take ENGL 1320 in the following semester). Students must receive a grade of C or higher in both courses to fulfill this core requirement.

requirements.name: Component Area Option double-dip rule
requirements.text: Note: Students may not “double-dip” courses to complete the University Core Curriculum. If a student completes for the Social and Behavioral Sciences area, PADM 2100 may not count toward Component Area Option A.

requirements.name: Option A other-core courses
requirements.text: Or any course included in the other core areas listed above (Communication, Life and Physical Sciences, etc.)

requirements.name: Other ways to complete the core
requirements.text: A student who successfully completes the common core curriculum at a state-assisted institution of higher education in Texas may transfer as “core complete” to UNT. The student will receive academic credit for each of the courses transferred. See also the UNT transfer articulation web page on the Registrar’s Office web site, where you can find information on the online transfer course equivalency tool Transferology. Certain core areas may be completed, fully or in part, by the successful completion of the appropriate advanced standing examination (AP/IB/CLEP). More information about advanced standing examinations accepted by UNT may be found on the Test, Prior Learning and Transfer Credit page under “Advanced Placement and Credit by Examination.” Please speak to your advisor to determine how an advanced standing examination may be used in meeting your degree requirements.
